# Grounded generator pilot -- AIMS-F

**Section 4 of the grounded-generator brief. Measured, not asserted.** Generated by
`scripts/gen-grounded-items.mjs` against `ISO/IEC 42001:2023` and formatted by
`scripts/emit-pilot-report.mjs` from `PILOT-GROUNDED-AIMSF.json`. Nothing in the live bank was touched: this
was a dry run, and the artifact is what `--apply --from=` would insert item for item.

## What the numbers are

| | |
|---|---|
| model | `claude-opus-5` |
| items attempted | 40, allocated across the domains by `weight_pct` |
| items the writer produced | 39 |
| **survivors** | **31** |
| rejected by a code gate | 7 |
| rejected by the blind solver | 1 |
| undecided (solver could not run) | 0 |
| tasks mapped to passages | 35 of 35 |


**How these items came to exist.** RAW WRITER OUTPUT, ungated and unsolved. Not a result. Generated in TWO PASSES: 31 items in the first, then 8 for the tasks a network outage cost (2.6, 4.7, 5.1-5.6 -- the whole of domain D5). Same library, same mapping, same gates; only the clock differs.

Allocation is by domain weight rather than evenly over tasks, because that is the basis
`generate-mock-exam` assembles a form on. A pilot spread evenly would over-sample the
light domains and say nothing about the shape of a real form.

## Why items were rejected

A single item can fail more than one gate, so these do not sum to the rejection count.

| n | gate |
|---|---|
| 4 | code: structure |
| 3 | code: modal-fidelity |
| 1 | solver: second defensible option |

**`solver COULD NOT RUN` is not a rejection and is never counted as one.** A step that
could not start is not a step that failed: folding it into the rejections would blame the
items for the transport, and folding it into the survivors would clear items nobody checked.

## The gates, and which of them is not a model

| gate | what it checks | model involved |
|---|---|---|
| `clause-exists` | every clause named is in the library, and is not a declared library gap | no |
| `verbatim` | `key_support` occurs **exactly** in the named passage | no |
| `modal-fidelity` | a `must` claim needs a `shall` anchor in a `shall` clause | no |
| `superseded-wording` | retired edition wording anywhere in the item | no |
| `structure` | cue guard, key-as-longest, odd-one-out by negation and by opening word | no |
| `near-duplicate` | share of the **shorter** stem's distinctive terms against live items on the same task | no |
| blind solver | is it solvable to the key from the passages, with no second defensible option | **yes, and it never sees the key** |

---

## Survivors

Each shows the anchor the item points at. **`key_support` is internal**: it is a sentence
copied out of a licensed standard as the evidence that the item is supported, and it is
never shown to a candidate, returned by a function, or served through MCP.

### 1. AIMS-F · D1 · task 1.1

**A candidate is asked to describe, in plain terms, what an "AI management system" is. Which description matches the defined meaning of a management system?**

- **`KEY` a) The organization's interrelated elements used to set policies and objectives, and the processes to achieve them**
- b) The defined set of activities for ongoing operation of an AI system, covering monitoring, repairs, updates and support
- c) The organization's process for assessing potential consequences of an AI system for individuals, groups and societies
- d) The body of technical documentation describing an AI system's purpose, assumptions, limitations and monitoring functions

*explanation:* Clause 3.4 defines a management system as the set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization used to establish policies and objectives, together with the processes to achieve those objectives; Note 2 adds structure, roles and responsibilities, planning and operation. The other options name specific AI-related activities or artefacts (operation and monitoring, impact assessment, technical documentation), not the management system itself.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 3.4:*

> set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization (3.1) to establish policies (3.5) and objectives (3.6), as well as processes (3.8) to achieve those objectives

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 3.2/3.4 defines a management system as the "set of interrelated or interacting elements of an organization to establish policies and objectives, as well as processes to achieve those objectives".

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 2. AIMS-F · D1 · task 1.2

**A company trains an AI model in-house, packages it as a hosted platform sold to client organizations, and also integrates third-party data feeds into it. Considering the organization's roles with respect to its AI systems, which statement best describes the position?**

- **`KEY` a) It can hold several roles at once, and its roles can affect applicability of requirements and controls.**
- b) Only one role can apply to an organization, so it must choose between being a provider and being a producer.
- c) The company must first document the AI management system scope and only afterwards consider any of its roles.
- d) Determining its roles is purely optional advice, so the company may leave role determination out altogether.

*explanation:* Clause 4.1 requires the organization to determine its roles with respect to its AI systems, lists roles that can include 'one or more of the following' (provider, producer, customer, partner, subject, relevant authority), and states that the organization's roles can determine the applicability and extent of applicability of the requirements and controls.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 4.1:*

> The organization’s roles can determine the applicability and extent of applicability of the requirements and controls in this document.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 4.1 states roles 'can include... one or more of the following' and that 'The organization's roles can determine the applicability and extent of applicability of the requirements and controls in this document.'

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 3. AIMS-F · D1 · task 1.3

**A deployed classification system is not retrained on production data, yet over several months its measured accuracy against production data declines, with no errors or failures logged. Which description best matches the guidance on AI system operation and monitoring?**

- a) The decline shows the system is operating as a continuously learning system, since production and output data are feeding back into the model.
- b) The decline is an error or failure condition, so it is addressed through the repair processes rather than through performance monitoring.
- **`KEY` c) Performance can change without continuous learning, usually from concept or data drift in production data, and monitoring can reveal a need for retraining.**
- d) Because continuous learning is not used, ongoing performance monitoring against production data is not among the minimum elements of operation.

*explanation:* B.6.2.6 states that the performance of some AI systems can change even where continuous learning is not used, usually because of concept or data drift in production data, and that in such cases monitoring can identify the need for retraining so the system continues to meet its design goals.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause B.6.2.6:*

> The performance of some AI systems can change even if such systems do not use continuous learning, usually due to concept or data drift in production data.

*blind solver:* answered C, no second defensible option — B.6.2.6 states that performance of some AI systems can change even without continuous learning, usually due to concept or data drift in production data, and that monitoring can identify the need for retraining.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 4. AIMS-F · D1 · task 1.4

**Annex D discusses using an AI management system together with an information security management system. According to that annex, what makes the combined use of ISO/IEC 42001 and ISO/IEC 27001 straightforward for an organization?**

- **`KEY` a) Both standards are built on the same high-level structure, so their integrated use is facilitated.**
- b) ISO/IEC 27001 is cited as a normative reference of this document, so parts of its content form requirements here.
- c) The risk criteria of the AI management system are drawn directly from ISO/IEC 27001, so only one risk process is run.
- d) Independent conformity assessment to ISO 9001 has to be completed first, which then aligns the two security-related systems.

*explanation:* Annex D.2 states that because both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management system use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit, and that security-related controls (see B.6.1.2) can be integrated with the organization's ISO/IEC 27001 implementation.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause D.2:*

> Given that both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management systems use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause D.2 states "Given that both ISO/IEC 27001 and the AI management systems use the high-level structure, their integrated use is facilitated and of great benefit for the organization."

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (17)

### 5. AIMS-F · D2 · task 2.1

**A retailer is adapting its existing ISO/IEC 27001 context analysis for a new AI management system. The draft lists supplier dependencies, data-centre resilience and applicable privacy law, and the team plans to leave it there. Which action best completes the context determination for the AIMS?**

- **`KEY` a) Add a determination of whether climate change is a relevant issue for the organization.**
- b) Restrict the issues considered to confidentiality, integrity and availability of information.
- c) Leave out the intended purpose of the AI systems, as purpose belongs in operational planning.
- d) Postpone deciding the organization's roles in relation to its AI systems until the scope statement is signed off.

*explanation:* Clause 4.1 adds an explicit determination that an information-security-shaped analysis typically omits: whether climate change is a relevant issue. The other options contradict the same clause, which also requires consideration of the AI systems' intended purpose and determination of the organization's roles.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 4.1:*

> The organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 4.1 explicitly states "The organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue", a requirement absent from the draft.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 6. AIMS-F · D2 · task 2.3

**An organization decides to merge two internal AI governance committees and rewrite several documented AIMS procedures. This is a change to the management system itself, not to an AI system in operation. Which requirement applies most directly to this decision?**

- **`KEY` a) The change must be carried out in a planned manner.**
- b) The change must be expressed as an AI objective that is measurable where practicable.
- c) The effectiveness of the change must be monitored as a control related to AI system operation, with corrective action considered.
- d) The change must be treated as an externally provided process and controlled on that basis.

*explanation:* Clause 6.3 covers changes to the AI management system itself and requires only that, once the need is determined, the changes be carried out in a planned manner. The other options draw on clauses addressing objectives (6.2) or operational planning and control (8.1), which concern operational processes and controls rather than a restructuring of the management system.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.3:*

> When the organization determines the need for changes to the AI management system, the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 6.3 states that when the organization determines the need for changes to the AI management system, the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner, which directly addresses a change to the AIMS itself.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 7. AIMS-F · D2 · task 2.5

**A financial services firm has run its standard IT risk assessment on a new credit-scoring AI system, covering confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data and infrastructure. The AI governance lead must now complete the analysis step of the organization's AI risk assessment process. Which additional analysis does the AIMS require at this step?**

- a) Compare the controls chosen for the identified risks against Annex A to confirm none necessary have been omitted
- **`KEY` b) Assess the consequences to the organization, to individuals and to societies if the identified risks materialize**
- c) Produce a statement of applicability listing the necessary controls, with justification for each inclusion and exclusion
- d) Review the AI policy at planned intervals to confirm its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness before proceeding

*explanation:* Clause 6.1.2 d) 1) requires the AI risk assessment process to analyse AI risks so as to assess the potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies should the risks materialize. This is the AI-specific dimension that a purely IT-asset-focused assessment (confidentiality, integrity, availability) would not surface. The other options belong to the risk treatment process (6.1.3) or to policy review guidance (B.2.4), not to the analysis step of the risk assessment.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1.2:*

> assess the potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies that would result if the identified risks were to materialize

*blind solver:* answered B, no second defensible option — Clause 6.1.2 d) 1) requires the analysis step of the AI risk assessment to assess the potential consequences to the organization, individuals and societies if identified risks materialize, going beyond standard IT confidentiality/integrity/availability concerns.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 8. AIMS-F · D2 · task 2.7

**A deployment team has completed and documented an AI system impact assessment for a new triage tool, covering deployment, intended use and foreseeable misuse in the relevant technical, societal and jurisdictional context. The AI governance lead now asks how this output relates to the AI risk assessment required for the same system. Which course of action is consistent with the management system requirements?**

- **`KEY` a) Take the impact assessment results into account in the risk assessment, which still determines risk levels and prioritises risks for treatment.**
- b) Treat the impact assessment as covering consequences to individuals and societies, so that the risk analysis only has to assess consequences to the organization.
- c) Publish the impact assessment to relevant interested parties, since this release is a precondition before the risk analysis can proceed.
- d) Rely on the documented impact assessment in place of retaining documented information about the risk assessment process.

*explanation:* Clause 6.1.4 makes the impact assessment an input to risk assessment ('shall consider the results ... in the risk assessment (see 6.1.2)'), while 6.1.2 e) keeps the risk assessment anchored to comparison with risk criteria and prioritization of risks for treatment. The two are separately required; the impact assessment feeds the risk assessment rather than replacing any part of it.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1.4:*

> The organization shall consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment (see 6.1.2).

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 6.1.4 requires that the organization 'shall consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment (see 6.1.2)', while 6.1.2 d)–e) still requires the risk assessment to determine levels of risk and prioritize risks for treatment.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 9. AIMS-F · D2 · task 2.8

**An AI development team has completed its risk treatment step. To implement one chosen treatment option it designed a control that does not appear in Annex A. It also concluded, from the risk assessment and a review of applicable external requirements, that one Annex A control is not needed. Under ISO/IEC 42001 6.1.3, how should these two outcomes be reflected?**

- **`KEY` a) Record both in the statement of applicability, justifying the inclusion of the organization-designed control and the exclusion of the Annex A control.**
- b) Record only the Annex A controls in the statement of applicability, since organization-designed controls sit outside its scope and are tracked in the treatment plan.
- c) Record the two controls and also document a justification for the items of Annex B implementation guidance that the organization decided not to follow.
- d) Record the organization-designed control with its justification, and simply omit the unneeded Annex A control, as only included controls carry a justification.

*explanation:* Clause 6.1.3 f) requires the statement of applicability to contain the necessary controls determined under b), c) and d) — which expressly includes controls additional to Annex A — together with justification for both inclusion and exclusion of controls; the grounds cited (not deemed necessary by the risk assessment, not required by applicable external requirements) are exactly the exclusion justifications the clause recognises.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 6.1.3:*

> f) produce a statement of applicability that contains the necessary controls [see b), c) and d)] and provide justification for inclusion and exclusion of controls.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 6.1.3 f) requires a statement of applicability containing the necessary controls [including additional controls identified under d)] with justification for both inclusion and exclusion of controls, and notes exclusion can be justified where the risk assessment or external requirements deem them unnecessary.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 10. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.1

**An organization deploying an AI-based triage tool staffs the project with three data scientists and one clinical domain expert. Reviewing the roles, the AIMS manager finds that no assigned person has the competence needed for the human oversight duties that affect AI performance. Applying the competence requirements of the AI management system, what is the organization required to do?**

- **`KEY` a) Take action to acquire the missing competence and then evaluate whether that action was effective.**
- b) Recruit an external oversight specialist, because mentoring or reassigning current employees cannot close a competence gap.
- c) Deliver an awareness briefing covering the AI policy and the implications of nonconformity, which closes a competence gap.
- d) Accept only formal academic qualifications as the basis for demonstrating the competence of these persons.

*explanation:* Clause 7.2 requires the organization to determine necessary competence for persons whose work affects AI performance and, where applicable, to take actions to acquire the necessary competence and evaluate the effectiveness of those actions; appropriate documented information is kept as evidence.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.2:*

> where applicable, take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 7.2 requires the organization, where applicable, to 'take actions to acquire the necessary competence, and evaluate the effectiveness of the actions taken'.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 11. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.2

**A certification candidate is asked to explain the awareness provision of the AI management system. Which statement best reflects it?**

- **`KEY` a) Anyone doing work under the organization's control is to be aware of the AI policy, their contribution to AIMS effectiveness, and the implications of non-conformity.**
- b) Only directly employed staff need awareness of the AI policy; contractors and other external workers are addressed solely through evidence of competence records.
- c) Awareness is satisfied only when documented information is retained for each person as evidence that the AI policy has been read and understood.
- d) Awareness concerns external communication with interested parties, so the organization determines what, when, with whom and how to communicate outside the organization only.

*explanation:* Clause 7.3 (Awareness) applies to persons doing work under the organization's control, not just employees, and lists exactly three awareness topics: the AI policy, contribution to the effectiveness of the AIMS including benefits of improved AI performance, and the implications of not conforming with AIMS requirements.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.3:*

> Persons doing work under the organization’s control shall be aware of: — the AI policy (see 5.2); — their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, including the benefits of improved AI performance; — the implications of not conforming with the AI management system requirements.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 7.3 states that persons doing work under the organization's control shall be aware of the AI policy, their contribution to the effectiveness of the AI management system, and the implications of not conforming.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 12. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.3

**An AIMS team uses a supplier's dataset documentation pack, obtained from outside the organization, and has determined it is necessary for planning and operating the AI management system. Applying the control of documented information requirements, what does the team have to do with this pack?**

- **`KEY` a) Identify it as appropriate and control it alongside internal documented information.**
- b) Leave it outside the AIMS documentation set, because only documents created inside the organization fall under document control.
- c) Share it with the relevant regulatory authority within the appropriate timeframe before it may be used in the AIMS.
- d) Have top management approve it at planned intervals as part of the review of the AI management system.

*explanation:* Clause 7.5.3 states that documented information of external origin determined by the organization to be necessary for the planning and operation of the AIMS shall be identified as appropriate and controlled, i.e. it is brought into the same control regime (distribution/access, storage, change control, retention) as internal documented information.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.5.3:*

> Documented information of external origin determined by the organization to be necessary for the planning and operation of the AI management system shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 7.5.3 states that documented information of external origin determined necessary for the planning and operation of the AI management system shall be identified as appropriate and controlled.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 13. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.4

**A provider outsources its training-data labelling activity to an external supplier. The labelling activity feeds an AI system that is in scope of the AI management system. Which statement best reflects the operational planning and control requirement that applies to this arrangement?**

- **`KEY` a) The outsourced labelling activity is relevant to the AI management system, so the organization has to ensure it is controlled.**
- b) Because the labelling is performed externally, the controls determined during risk treatment apply only to activities performed in-house.
- c) Records showing the labelling process ran as planned need only be produced if the external supplier asks the organization for them.
- d) Monitoring of control effectiveness for the supplier is deferred to the internal audit programme, and corrective action is considered only when an auditor raises a finding.

*explanation:* Clause 8.1 states that externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the AI management system are to be controlled by the organization; outsourcing the activity does not remove it from the scope of operational control.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 8.1:*

> The organization shall ensure that externally provided processes, products or services that are relevant to the AI management system are controlled.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 8.1 states that "The organization shall ensure that externally provided processes, products or services that are relevant to the AI management system are controlled."

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 14. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.5

**A retailer licenses a pre-trained ranking model from a vendor and embeds it in its customer-facing app. Post-deployment monitoring shows the model is not performing as intended and is producing outcomes that conflict with the retailer's stated responsible-AI approach. According to the Annex B guidance on suppliers, what is the appropriate response regarding the vendor?**

- **`KEY` a) Call on the vendor to take corrective actions; the retailer can choose to work with the vendor to achieve this.**
- b) Treat the matter as closed once the retailer has documented how the vendor's model is integrated into its own AI system.
- c) Accept the behaviour as an inherent technical limitation of a bought-in component and simply record it in the AI system technical documentation supplied to users.
- d) Raise the monitoring and evaluation requirements applied to every supplier to the same uniform maximum level, irrespective of what each supplier provides or the risk it poses.

*explanation:* B.10.3 states that where supplied AI systems or components do not perform as intended or lead to impacts misaligned with the organization's responsible approach, the organization should require the supplier to take corrective actions, and it can decide to work with the supplier to achieve this.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause B.10.3:*

> Where the organization considers that the AI system or AI system components from a supplier do not perform as intended or can result in impacts to individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies that are not aligned with the responsible approach to AI systems taken by the organization, the organization should require the supplier to take corrective actions.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause B.10.3 states that where supplier-provided AI system components do not perform as intended or produce impacts not aligned with the organization's responsible AI approach, the organization should require the supplier to take corrective actions and can decide to work with the supplier to achieve this.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 15. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.6

**Guidance on data management for AI system development lists several data properties. Which of the following is a data property that bears on whether the AI system behaves as intended in its setting of use, rather than one of the properties that information security is defined as preserving?**

- **`KEY` a) Representativeness of training data compared to the operational domain of use**
- b) Confidentiality of the information used, which is one of the properties that the definition of information security preserves
- c) Availability of the information used, which is one of the properties that the definition of information security preserves
- d) Integrity of the information used, which is one of the properties that the definition of information security preserves

*explanation:* B.7.2 lists representativeness of training data compared to the operational domain of use among the topics that data management can include; it concerns how well the data reflects the domain the system operates in and is not one of the properties named in the definition of information security in 3.23 (confidentiality, integrity, availability).

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause B.7.2:*

> representativeness of training data compared to operational domain of use

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — B.7.2 lists “representativeness of training data compared to operational domain of use” as a data management topic bearing on fitness for the setting of use, whereas confidentiality, integrity and availability are the properties preserved per the information security definition in 3.23.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 16. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.7

**An organization with a mature, certified ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS is standing up an AI management system. Its ISMS already has a document control procedure, an internal/external communication plan, an annual security awareness programme, a competence matrix for security roles, and operational control procedures for security processes. Which conclusion about what carries over is best supported by the AIMS requirements?**

- **`KEY` a) The competence element has to be worked out again for persons whose work affects AI performance, with documented evidence of that competence.**
- b) The ISMS operational control procedures transfer as they stand, because the controls to be implemented are the same set in both systems.
- c) The security awareness programme transfers untouched, because awareness content does not depend on which management system is in place.
- d) The existing ISMS scope statement covers the AI management system unchanged, because the organizational boundaries have not moved.

*explanation:* Clause 7.2 ties competence determination to work that affects AI performance and requires documented information as evidence of competence; the body of knowledge and the evidence are therefore not the ISMS security competence set, so this element must be rebuilt rather than inherited.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 7.2:*

> determine the necessary competence of person(s) doing work under its control that affects its AI performance

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 7.2 requires the organization to determine the necessary competence of persons doing work that affects its AI performance, ensure competence, and keep documented information as evidence, so the competence element must be redone for AI roles.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 17. AIMS-F · D3 · task 3.8

**An organization operating a certified AI management system proposes extending an in-service AI system to a new customer segment and jurisdiction. The change has been approved in principle but has not yet been implemented, and the next scheduled review of assessments is eight months away. Under Clause 8, what is the correct course of action for the AI risk assessment?**

- **`KEY` a) Carry out an AI risk assessment now, because a significant change is proposed, and retain the documented results.**
- b) Wait until the change has actually been implemented in production before any AI risk assessment is carried out.
- c) Rely on the next planned-interval assessment in eight months, since planned intervals are the only trigger stated.
- d) Record any newly identified risks in the statement of applicability, instead of running the risk treatment process for them.

*explanation:* Clause 8.2 requires AI risk assessments to be performed at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur, so a proposed (not yet implemented) significant change is itself a trigger; 8.2 also requires documented information of the results of all AI risk assessments to be retained.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 8.2:*

> The organization shall perform AI risk assessments in accordance with 6.1.2 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 8.2 requires AI risk assessments 'at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur' and that documented information of the results be retained, so the proposed (not yet implemented) change triggers an assessment now.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 18. AIMS-F · D4 · task 4.1

**An AIMS coordinator asks how the Annex B implementation guidance relates to the statement of applicability. Which description matches the standard?**

- **`KEY` a) Its inclusion or exclusion need not be justified in the statement of applicability.**
- b) Each item of guidance an organization adopts has to be listed and justified in the statement of applicability.

- d) The guidance covers only a selected subset of the Table A.1 controls, chiefly those on AI system life cycle.

*explanation:* B.1 states that the guidance supports implementation of the Table A.1 controls, but organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability.

> It provides information to support the implementation of the controls listed in Table A.1 and to meet the control objective, but organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability (see 6.1.3).

### 19. AIMS-F · D4 · task 4.2

Which Annex B life-cycle control category most directly addresses this gap?**

*explanation:* B.6.2.6 covers the ongoing operation of a deployed AI system, with system and performance monitoring, repairs, updates and support as the minimum elements, and it expressly anticipates performance change from concept or data drift in production data, where monitoring can identify the need for retraining. ### 25. AIMS-F · D4 · task 4.7

**An organization certified to ISO/IEC 27001 maps an AI Annex A data provenance control to its existing 27001 access control on the deployed model's inference endpoint, and records in the Statement of Applicability that the AI control is "satisfied by the ISMS". Which analysis of this mapping is best supported by the standard?**

- a) The mapping is sound, because Annex D.2 states that an organization with an ISO/IEC 27001 implementation may treat any AI control touching data as already implemented through the ISMS.
- b) The mapping is sound, because once the security-related AI controls are integrated with the ISMS, the associated risks and controls no longer need to be reflected in the Statement of Applicability.
- **`KEY` c) The mapping is unsound: endpoint access control addresses security, whereas the provenance control looks for a documented process for recording where the data came from.**
- d) The mapping cannot be assessed, because the Annex B implementation guidance for data provenance would first have to be documented and justified for inclusion or exclusion in the Statement of Applicability.

*explanation:* B.7.5 sets a distinct objective: a defined, documented process for recording data provenance over the life cycles of the data and the AI system. Annex D.2 only contemplates integrating controls that (partly) relate to information security with the ISO/IEC 27001 implementation; an access control on an endpoint protects the deployed system, it does not record the origin and handling history of the training data. Overlap with ISO/IEC 27001 is therefore not equivalence for this control pair.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause B.7.5:*

> The organization should define and document a process for recording the provenance of data used in its AI systems over the life cycles of the data and the AI system.

*blind solver:* answered C, no second defensible option — B.7.5 requires a documented process for recording the provenance of data (creation, update, transcription, validation, transfer of control) over the data and AI system life cycles, which an access control on an inference endpoint does not deliver; D.2 only supports integrating controls that (partly) relate to information security.

### 27. AIMS-F · D5 · task 5.2

**An organization plans an internal audit of its AI risk assessment process and appoints, as sole auditor, the manager who designed and runs that process. Under the internal audit programme clause, which requirement is most directly compromised by this assignment?**

- **`KEY` a) Auditors are to be selected so that the audit process stays objective and impartial.**
- b) Internal audits have to be carried out by an external party acting on the organization's behalf.
- c) Audit results are to be made public to all interested parties instead of being given to managers.
- d) Findings of previous audits are to be excluded when the audit programme is established.

*explanation:* Clause 9.2.2 b) requires the organization to select auditors and conduct audits in a way that ensures objectivity and impartiality of the audit process. An auditor auditing a process he or she designed and operates cannot evaluate it impartially, so this is the requirement at risk.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 9.2.2:*

> The organization shall: a) define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit; b) select auditors and conduct audits to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process; c) ensure that the results of audits are reported to relevant managers.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 9.2.2 b) requires the organization to 'select auditors and conduct audits to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process', which is directly breached by having the process owner audit his own process.

### 29. AIMS-F · D5 · task 5.4

**A deployed credit-scoring model begins producing invalid outputs after an upstream feature table is populated with stale records. The team immediately switches the model back to the previous version so the bad outputs stop. Under the AIMS nonconformity and corrective action requirements, which of the following is the corrective action, as distinct from the actions already taken?**

- a) Switch the model back to the previous version so the invalid outputs stop straight away.
- **`KEY` b) Determine what caused the stale data and check whether other models using that pipeline could fail the same way.**
- c) Notify the affected applicants, manually re-run every invalid decision, and issue corrected outcomes to everyone impacted by the failure.
- d) Record the nature of the failure in the incident log and file it with the audit evidence for the next review.

*explanation:* Clause 10.2 b) separates reaction/correction from corrective action: corrective action is the evaluation of the need for action to eliminate the cause(s) so the nonconformity does not recur or occur elsewhere, carried out by reviewing the nonconformity, determining its causes, and determining if similar nonconformities exist or can potentially occur. Investigating the stale-data cause and checking other models on the same pipeline is exactly that. Clause 3.17 likewise defines corrective action as action to eliminate the cause(s) and prevent recurrence.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 10.2:*

> b) evaluate the need for action to eliminate the cause(s) of the nonconformity, so that it does not recur or occur elsewhere, by: 1) reviewing the nonconformity; 2) determining the causes of the nonconformity; 3) determining if similar nonconformities exist or can potentially occur;

*blind solver:* answered B, no second defensible option — Clause 10.2 b) defines corrective action as evaluating the need to eliminate the cause(s) so the nonconformity does not recur or occur elsewhere — reviewing the nonconformity, determining its causes and determining if similar nonconformities exist or can potentially occur — while 3.17 defines corrective action as eliminating the cause and preventing recurrence.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

### 30. AIMS-F · D5 · task 5.5

**A certification consultant is explaining how audit frequency works under the AI management system standard. Which statement is consistent with the standard's internal audit clause?**

- **`KEY` a) The organization itself sets how often internal audits occur, as part of establishing its audit programme.**

- d) Audit results may be retained internally only and need not be reported to relevant managers.

*explanation:* Clause 9.2.2 places the audit programme, expressly including its frequency, with the organization. Nothing in the clause hands frequency to an external certifier; requirements on bodies that audit and certify management systems sit in separate documents, not in this standard.

> The organization shall plan, establish, implement and maintain (an) audit programme(s), including the frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 9.2.2 requires the organization to plan, establish, implement and maintain audit programme(s) 'including the frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting', so the organization sets audit frequency.

### 31. AIMS-F · D5 · task 5.6

**An organization runs one integrated internal audit programme covering both its ISMS and its AI management system. For the AIMS part, the audit team offers the organization's AI system impact assessment records as the evidence of risk assessment, and notes that audit results were discussed only in the management review. Which analysis of this evidence position is correct?**

- **`KEY` a) Impact assessment results feed the risk assessment, but retained results of AI risk assessments are still needed.**
- b) A single combined audit is not acceptable; the ISMS and the AIMS have to be audited as two separate audits with separate reports.
- c) Documented information is only needed for the audit results themselves, so no record of the audit programme's implementation is expected.
- d) Reporting audit results to relevant managers is satisfied entirely by tabling them as an input to the management review.

*explanation:* Clause 6.1.4 states that the results of the AI system impact assessment are to be considered in the risk assessment (6.1.2); the impact assessment is therefore an input, not a substitute. Clause 8.2 independently requires AI risk assessments in accordance with 6.1.2 and retention of documented information of the results of all AI risk assessments, so both record sets are needed.

*`key_support` — ISO/IEC 42001 clause 8.2:*

> The organization shall perform AI risk assessments in accordance with 6.1.2 at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur. The organization shall retain documented information of the results of all AI risk assessments.

*blind solver:* answered A, no second defensible option — Clause 6.1.4 requires the organization to consider impact assessment results in the risk assessment, while 8.2/6.1.2 separately require AI risk assessments at planned intervals with documented information of the results of all AI risk assessments retained, so impact assessment records cannot substitute for risk assessment records.

*gates:* clause-exists pass (4) · verbatim pass (4) · modal-fidelity pass (1) · superseded-wording pass (6) · structure pass (4) · near-duplicate pass (18)

- d) AI policy

*claimed anchor — clause B.2.3:* `The organization should determine where other policies can be affected by or apply to, the organization’s objectives with respect to AI systems.`

- **blind solver** rejected: the solver picked the key but calls A defensible: B.2.4 notes the AI policy review should assess opportunities for improvement of the organization's policies in response to changes, which a candidate could argue covers the gap, though it targets the AI policy itself rather than other policies.

---

## What this pilot does not show

- **Tier A and Tier B rates are a HUMAN READ, and this report is not one.** The target was
  zero Tier A and a Tier B rate well under 9%. Nothing here can claim either: a Tier A
  finding is a wrong key, and the instrument that establishes a key is wrong is somebody
  reading the item against the standard. What the gates establish is narrower and worth
  saying exactly: every survivor points at a real sentence in a pinned edition, the
  sentence says what the item claims it says at the strength the item claims, and a model
  that never saw the key reached the key from the passages alone.
- **A DEFINITION CLAUSE'S `normative` CLASS IS THE WEAKEST THING IN THE LIBRARY.** The
  extractor classes a passage by the strongest modal in its own text, which is right for a
  requirement clause and crude for a terms-and-definitions entry: a definition whose note
  contains the word *can* is classed `can`, and a definition imposes nothing at all. One
  rejection in this run turns on that (clause 3.2). Refusing is still the right direction --
  an item may not say *should* on the authority of a definition -- but the class is a proxy
  and `informative` would describe those rows better.
- **The near-duplicate gate compares stems.** Two items with different stems and the same
  answer are invisible to it -- which is exactly the eight near-duplicate pairs the
  480-item audit found by reading. A threshold cannot find those.
- **A dry run of a generator is a sample, not a preview.** A second run writes different
  items. These are the items that were gated, because the artifact was persisted first.
- **The library is PARTIAL where it says so.** No item was refused for naming a missing clause in this run.

## The comparison the decision actually needs

This report cannot be read against the old generator on its own. The old path's error rate
is known from a human read -- 16 wrong keys in 822 items, 1.9% -- and the equivalent number
for these survivors requires the same instrument: somebody reading them against ISO/IEC
42001:2023. The survivors above are laid out in `AUDIT-SAMPLE.md`'s format so that read can
happen the same way, and each one carries the sentence it rests on so the reading is against
the standard's own words rather than against recall.
